We head to the Bolivian border and start our 4×4 tour. You’ll see Laguna Verde and take in panoramic views of Licancabur Volcano. The route passes the monumental rock formations of the Dalí Valley and the Polques hot springs before reaching the active geysers of Sol de Mañana, where you can watch hot mud erupt. Our next stop is Laguna Colorada, a red lake in Bolivia at 4,400 m above sea level. Rare James’s flamingos come here to feed on a type of plankton found in abundance in the lake.
We spend the night at an expedition-style hotel in the desert.
The route reaches elevations above 4,000 m, where altitude sickness is possible.
Pink flamingos in the red waters of Laguna Colorada, Bolivia
Laguna Colorada: flamingos by the white mineral shore and dry mountains
04.11 · Lagoons and the Chiguana and Uyuni Salt Flats

After breakfast, we head for the smaller lagoons of Honda, Chiarkota, Hedionda and Cañapa, with a stop at the Ollagüe Volcano viewpoint. The volcano is still active, and you can see smoke rising from its crater. We then cross the Chiguana Salt Flats, known for their large deposits of sodium and potassium nitrates.
Next we visit Salar de Uyuni, the world’s largest dried-up salt lake. It lies on a high plateau in southern Bolivia at 3,650 m above sea level and covers around 11,000 sq km. At the centre, the salt crust is up to 10 m thick. In the dry season, the lake is a vast salt desert holding an estimated 10 billion tonnes of salt. In the rainy season, a shallow layer of water turns it into the world’s largest mirror.
On the way to the salt flats, you’ll see how salt is extracted and processed in Colchani. We then visit the Ojos de Agua, where you can see local geological formations and watch salt being processed. On Fish Island, you’ll see several giant cacti and have views across the flats. A boxed lunch is included.
Transfer to Uyuni at the end of the tour.
